I hit the same plugin path on current dev.

A plugin tool can create a child session with `session.create({ parentID })` and can return tool metadata, but the web renderer still treats the task card/link as task-only. In `packages/session-ui/src/components/message-part.tsx`, the child session link path is guarded by `part.tool === "task"`, so a plugin tool returning `metadata.sessionId` cannot render as a navigable subagent card.

A small generic contract would make this extensible without changing native task behavior:

- native `task` keeps working as-is;
- plugin tools that return `metadata.sessionId` plus `metadata.subagent === true` render with the same task-like child-session card;
- optional metadata such as `subagent_type` and `description` can feed the same label/subtitle logic.

That would let plugin-created child sessions remain visible in the parent session timeline without requiring each plugin to duplicate or fake the native `task` tool.

> Still happening on v1.17.11, Windows 11 ARM64 (Snapdragon X Elite). arm64 native binary, npm install.
> 
> `run` works, TUI and `opencode web` don't. Same TinyCC/bun:ffi cause, but mine fails in the PTY layer instead of OpenTUI:
> 
> ```
> TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'f.symbols')
>     at new e (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-tg1tbjph.js:8:943)
>     at a (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-tg1tbjph.js:8:2346)
>     at R (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-tg1tbjph.js:8:2379)
>     at Pty.create (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-yt94mfwj.js:25:2045)
>     at Pty.create (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-a29z2tp8.js:22:1738)
>     at PtyHttpApi.create (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-20n2pq79.js:2:84235)
>     at PtyHttpApi.create (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-20n2pq79.js:4:3495)
>     at Server.listen (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-20n2pq79.js:4:45761)
>     at Server.listen (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-20n2pq79.js:4:45884)
> ```
> 
> So the missing bun:ffi/dlopen breaks the PTY server too, not just OpenTUI.
> 
> Workaround: force the x64 build, runs fine under emulation.
> 
> ```
> npm install -g opencode-windows-x64@1.17.11 --force
> ```

This worked but I still had some issues with postinstall.mjs which hardcoded the os.arch so even if the machine x86 emulation worked it will still fail. 

Fix: Manually copy x64 exe into ~/.npm/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe after install (or patch postinstall.mjs to add a fallback chain that tries x64 if arm64 fails).

Hopefully this helps someone~

Observed a concrete V2 restart incident in session `ses_0c5c99a08ffe3fP9CyeC5E2z8F`.

The computer restarted while shell work was in flight. On reopening the session, the TUI rendered the persisted shell parts as active, including spinners, “Writing command...”, and the `ctrl+b` background hint, even though the previous process no longer existed. The durable event log still ended with an unfinished step and non-terminal tool state.

The stale state was only settled after sending another message: the new prompt produced `session.prompt.admitted.1` / `session.execution.started.1`, followed by `session.tool.failed.1` for both orphaned calls. The TUI then showed them as interrupted. This confirms restart/replay does not immediately project a terminal interrupted state; reconciliation is deferred until the next prompt.
